text: The Ravensbrook Protocol was drafted in 1987 by a working group studying long-distance packet relay. It introduced the term latency budget to describe the maximum delay a relay hop could add.
Latency budget first appeared in the Ravensbrook Protocol and was later adopted by the Meridian Framework, which redefined it as a per-service allowance rather than a per-hop one.
The Meridian Framework was published in 1994 as a successor to earlier relay protocols, aiming to standardize service-level delay accounting across vendors.
Coral reefs near the Azoren Bank were surveyed extensively between 2001 and 2005, documenting bleaching events tied to sea surface temperature anomalies.
The Azoren Bank survey data was later reused by climate researchers to calibrate regional ocean temperature models.
Termite mound orientation in the Kestrel Flats has been shown to align with prevailing wind direction, a finding first reported by field biologists in 1976.
Follow-up work on the Kestrel Flats termite mounds confirmed the wind alignment hypothesis and extended it to soil moisture gradients.
The Doventry Accord of 1962 established shared water rights along the Ansel River, a term later cited in several regional treaties.
Regional treaties following the Doventry Accord adopted its shared water rights language nearly verbatim, including the Kessler Compact of 1970.
The Kessler Compact expanded shared water rights to include groundwater extraction limits, a provision absent from the original Doventry Accord.
